title: Armenia
subtitle: to the shores of Lake Sevan
standfirst: A route through Armenia and Nagorno-Karabakh in August 2015, when Karabakh was a disputed territory run by a self-declared Armenian republic. These are the photos from that week, looked at again ten years on.

stops.caption: Stepanakert, then the capital of the self-declared republic. On the hill above the town stands We Are Our Mountains (1967), an elderly couple carved in tuff, known locally as Tatik-Papik, “grandmother and grandfather”. The city is now Khankendi, its Azerbaijani name.

note.title: Karabakh in 2015, and since
paras: Nagorno-Karabakh is internationally recognised as part of Azerbaijan. In 2015 it was run by a self-declared republic, known to Armenians as Artsakh, which no country recognised, including Armenia. It had held the region and a belt of surrounding Azerbaijani districts since the war of 1988–1994 ended in a ceasefire.

The only way in was by road from Armenia, usually through the Lachin corridor from Goris, with an entry permit from the de facto authorities. Azerbaijan regarded visits made this way, without its permission, as a breach of its law, and could bar foreigners who made them from entering the country.

In the autumn of 2020 a six-week war returned the surrounding districts, including Kalbajar beyond the Sotk Pass, and part of Karabakh itself to Azerbaijan. In September 2023 an Azerbaijani military operation ended the republic’s control, and within about a week more than 100,000 Armenians, almost the entire population, left for Armenia. The republic was formally dissolved on 1 January 2024, and the whole region is now governed by Azerbaijan.
These photographs were taken before all of that. Where a place has two names, I use both.

stops.caption: Gandzasar monastery in the Khachen valley, north of Stepanakert. Its church of St John the Baptist was consecrated in 1240.

photos.alt: The carved drum and conical roof of Gandzasar church against a blue sky
The long rubble-stone monastery wall with arched wooden doors and small windows

stops.caption: Out of Karabakh by the northern road, through the Kalbajar district and over the Sotk Pass into Armenia, down to Vardenis. Kalbajar returned to Azerbaijani control in November 2020.

photos.alt: Cattle standing and lying on a gravel mountain road between forested slopes
Soviet apartment blocks with washing on the balconies, a wide plain and mountains behind

stops.caption: Sevanavank, above Lake Sevan. The lake later became the subject of my score.
